10-15 years is around the maximum I think BTC (as we know it) will continue to exist. More if its mcap goes to tens of trillions (energy price (~inflation) adjusted), less if the price dumps hard. On Silver and Gold price fluctuations: an effortpost

Open thread • Replies: 11 • Updated: 2026-10-20 23:40 UTC

OP

Silver and gold have intrensic cash value. They can be held as a form of non-cash reserves, while remaining highly liquid, and are owned either physically or as a share in a depository, or as a futures contract, without a significant difference in purchase price, sale price or underlying asset value.

Gold and Silver, for over 90% of owners are a form and means of SAVINGS.

Gold and silver are NOT
>a growth stock
>a get rich quick scheme
>a passive income stream
Gold and Silver are a global piggy bank, with real demand and therefore real value today.

>but muh stocks and bonds
Yes, they have a great deal of momentum behind them, and you can make a lot of money with them. You should. Making money on a bond or a stock dividend is a good idea. The whole of the financial world is built around drawing money into stocks and bonds, because that's how banks get paid, so if you are smart and lucky you should do very well with them.

Gold and Silver are not intended to function that way.

When debt crashes a financial sector, such as subprime cars, which are imploding right now, the value of all credit related instruments becomes suspect, and the effects can be felt all over the world, from pensions and 401ks to hedge funds and on and on, and many banks and sovereign wealth funds can also be damaged, because to invest in a debt backed security, is to gamble in league with the bank. The bank touches everything and everyone that it can, and is, not hyperbolocally, but literally is, the Bank IS THE SYSTEM.

The system that everyone likes to sneer at and badmouth groan over, that system has a name: The Bank.

When the 2007-8 crisis happened, if you recall, all the high end institutions were effected, and the only ones out of danger were those which had never participated or associated with those institutions which had.

At the time there was a draw down in gold and silver prices, followed by a price rise over the next few years.
>ah see it dropped

Yes, because Gold and Silver are a piggy bank. As institutions needed fast money, they could, and did, sell of billions in gold reserves to raise immediate cash, because the demand for gold on the world market, generally speaking is 100%. If you need to sell it all, you can. Meanwhile, if you want to hold real value in an uninflatable asset, you can park money in Gold and Silver for your whole life, and it doesn't go bad, expire, or require any special licensure to acquire or liquidate. Moreover, because it is a physical asset you can have it in your own hand, you can transport it, you can divide it up, swap it around or trade it at your whim. And finally, because it is a finished good, and real people must do work to produce it, unlike financial instruments, it has a real underlying value, which, being tied to general inflation, cannot go to nothing.

If you forsee inflation, and want to save your purchasing power, in something not exposed to debt, then you can get gold and be reasonably certain that in 10 or 20 years, the work required to produce an ounce of gold or silver will be roughly equivelant to what is required now. It is the work, by the way, not strictly the material, which gives gold and silver it's value. The value, therefore, remains, without regard to politics or currency used to purchase the metal, it can be traded when where and how you choose. Foreseeing trouble, you can protect yourself from the destruction of purchasing power in currency by holding gold, which is simultaneously valuable in all currencies. In that sense it represents the best aspect of all currencies.

Gold Is All Currencies.
